findings.title: main()'s exit-code behavior changed but its own docstring still claims exit 3 unconditionally
locations: src/CLI/Main.jl:147-154 (the new `err isa Config.ConfigError && (...); return 2` branch)
src/CLI/Main.jl:115-124 (the unmodified `main(args) -> Int` docstring, both at base and head)
findings.before:
catch err
    println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": crashed — ", sprint(showerror, err))
    Base.show_backtrace(stderr, catch_backtrace()); println(stderr)
    return 3
end
findings.after:
catch err
    # A structurally bad config is the documented exit 2 — "cannot evaluate" — and not a crash: ...
    err isa Config.ConfigError && (println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": ", sprint(showerror, err)); return 2)
    println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": crashed — ", sprint(showerror, err))
    Base.show_backtrace(stderr, catch_backtrace()); println(stderr)
    return 3
end
findings.why_it_matters: Every `gbg <noun> <verb>` invocation not already wrapped by `design_verb` or `Doctor`'s own local catch now returns exit 2 instead of exit 3 for a hand-edited/invalid `.gbg/config.toml`. Exit codes are this package's stated contract (CLAUDE.md: "Exit codes are the contract; a log is never grepped for a verdict"), and any external script, hook or CI step that branches on 3 = crash vs 2 = cannot-evaluate for one of the many verbs that used to hit the generic catch will now see a different code for the same failure. The fix is well-scoped (only `Config.ConfigError`, which Config.jl raises exclusively for absent/unparsable/schema-invalid/path-invalid config) and it corrects behavior to match what `main()`'s docstring already promised ("2 cannot evaluate ... 3 crash") — but that same docstring, two lines below, still says unconditionally "An exception escaping a verb is printed with its backtrace to stderr and returns 3", which the code no longer does for this class. The docstring is the reader-visible statement of the contract, and it was left saying the old thing while the code now does the new thing.
findings.description: The change itself is a justified, narrowly-scoped bug fix — it makes every verb's exit code match the pre-existing documented contract instead of only the three verbs that special-cased `ConfigError` themselves — but the diff does not update `main()`'s own docstring, which still states unconditionally that an escaping exception returns 3 with a backtrace. That statement is now false for `Config.ConfigError`. No test in this diff exercises the new branch either (test/coverage.jl is the only test file touched, and it is unrelated). A reader who consults the one docstring that documents this exit-code contract would not learn that this class of failure now returns 2 without a backtrace.
findings.evidence: Base main() docstring (git show af1adec6c6666be0c687ffd32bbc9145fecef580:src/CLI/Main.jl): "An exception escaping a verb is printed with its backtrace to `stderr` and returns 3, so a crash is never read as a finding" — unchanged at head, while the code added: "err isa Config.ConfigError && (println(stderr, "gbg ", key, ": ", sprint(showerror, err)); return 2)" before the unconditional `return 3` path.
